🚨Massive Epic Post from @litigious_dulce 🚨
🚨This IS NOT my work, helping him out due to technical difficulties🚨
🚨One of the most Epic $IREN posts you'll read about CSP potential!!!🚨

Part 1/2

INTRODUCTION

I will try to be as concise as possible, but this thread shall be long and slightly unorganized. Topics will include bitcoin mining, CSP, rack density, GPU clusters, neoclouds, etc. For my own convenience, I will also use Chatgpt for much of the writing. Thank God for AI.

BITCOIN MINING AND CSP:

TLDR: Iren is using Bitcoin mining as a means to quickly monetize its data centers, enabling it to build a large infrastructure portfolio suitable for AI/HPC without sacrificing equity or accumulating significant debt, positioning it as a resilient, vertically integrated alternative to heavily leveraged neocloud competitors.
—-
Iren’s motto is “Proceed with Purpose” for a reason. As reiterated in the Iren Q2 FY25 presentation, Iren’s plan has always been to transition from bitcoin mining to broader data center and AI infrastructure services. The three steps enumerated by Iren represent a methodical evolution: first, building data centers powered by low-cost renewable energy; second, bootstrapping operations with Bitcoin mining; and third, leveraging the resulting asset base into other high-growth, energy-intensive computing applications like AI cloud services.

Iren initially focused on constructing data centers where operational costs are minimized by tapping into cheap, renewable energy sources. Electricity is one of the largest expenses for data centers, so building facilities in areas rich with hydro, solar, or wind power ensures low ongoing costs and sustainable operations. As a result, Iren now owns significant amounts of land and physical infrastructure.

To monetize its newly constructed data centers, Iren bootstrapped (i.e., starting and growing the business using internally generated resources rather than relying on outside funding like debt or large investment rounds) operations through Bitcoin mining. This approach was strategic because ASIC miners, the specialized machines used for Bitcoin mining, generate revenue almost immediately after being plugged into the network. There is no customer acquisition risk; as soon as the machines are operational, they begin earning Bitcoin, which can be sold for cash. CSP, on the other hand, requires building a customer base, negotiating contracts, and maintaining high utilization — all of which introduce sales and marketing complexity.

In general, Bitcoin mining typically requires much lower capital expenditure (capex) than AI or HPC data centers. That said, Iren’s existing data centers (e.g., over 150 MW in Canada) are configured for both bitcoin mining and high-density AI workloads, with rack densities of about 80 kW. Despite this, Iren achieved construction costs of around $650,000 per megawatt, far below the $6–15 million per megawatt common for specialized AI facilities. Iren’s designs are not only extremely fast to build, but also easily retrofitted (e.g., the rack density should be scalable to 300 kW and beyond), giving Iren a significant advantage in flexibility and time to market (e.g., with respect to the B200s).
This efficient, infrastructure-first approach has allowed Iren to grow without taking on significant debt (in fact, Iren has no debt at the moment). In contrast, most neocloud competitors, such as CoreWeave, have funded their rapid expansion by raising large amounts of debt. Unlike Iren, most neoclouds typically own little land or physical infrastructure, which may stunt future growth.

Iren’s methodical strategy — building out low-cost, high-density infrastructure first through Bitcoin mining and then expanding into AI compute — positions it as a more resilient, vertically integrated player. Its strong asset base, low operational costs, and limited reliance on external financing give Iren a structurally more profitable and lower-risk business model compared to the heavily leveraged, asset-light models of many newer cloud providers.

IRENS’ DATA CENTERS
TLDR: Iren’s technical innovations validated its cost and speed strategy and has positioned it to now enter the AI and HPC markets quickly and profitably, without having to rebuild its infrastructure from scratch. Its ability to combine low-cost construction, high rack density, and air cooling into a unified platform is a major differentiator at a time when many competitors are struggling with expensive and slow transitions to liquid-cooled architectures.
—-
In 2018, Iren acquired PodTech, as well as all of the IP that had been transferred to it from RackForce (see nitter.poast.org/TheKamaHsutra/status/1… ). Around 2020, Iren designed and constructed a next-gen data center. However, this begs the question: what exactly constitutes a next-gen data center? Very few possessed the foresight in 2020 to anticipate ChatGPT (otherwise, we would all be billionaires from buying call options on $Nvda ). Iren apparently believed that essential features of a next-gen data center comprise being 1) affordable and fast to build; 2) capable of achieving high rack density; and 3) easy to retrofit. In addition, Iren wanted the data center to support bitcoin mining to bootstrap operations as described above.

Iren put this philosophy into practice by designing and constructing data centers at a relatively low cost of approximately $650,000/MW. At the same time, Iren engineered its facilities to achieve rack densities of up to 80 kilowatts, all while remaining air-cooled. Although widely dismissed by retail and even institutional investors, this air-cooled, high-density design is a major technical and strategic breakthrough. 

Traditionally, the industry consensus has been that air cooling becomes insufficient above 30 kW per rack. Beyond that point, most operators assume that liquid cooling — either direct-to-chip or full immersion — becomes necessary to prevent overheating and maintain reliability. Liquid cooling infrastructure, however, is significantly more expensive, adds construction complexity, and greatly increases build times (e.g., by months if not more than a year).

By radically improving air cooling system design, Iren proved that it was possible to almost triple traditional air-cooled rack densities without resorting to costly and complex liquid cooling solutions. This breakthrough allowed them to avoid the massive capital expenditure and long construction timelines typically associated with liquid-cooled data centers, giving them a huge advantage in both cost and speed to market.

While Iren was building these data centers and bootstrapping operations with bitcoin mining, most data center operators were investing heavily in liquid cooling retrofits or new builds under the assumption that air cooling simply could not scale to meet the demands of next-generation AI and HPC workloads. Iren’s decision to challenge this consensus was seen as risky; however, in hindsight, we know now that Iren’s existing data centers can not only host H100s and H200s, but also B200s without any material modification or retrofit to the design.

RACK DENSITY
TLDR: Although HGX B200 servers can technically run in low-density racks (the lowest possible rack density being 15 kW, which is above the average data center rack density of 12 kW), doing so wastes physical space, cooling, and networking resources because only one or two servers fit per rack. By contrast, Iren’s high-density racks (70–80 kW) allow four to five HGX B200 servers per rack, maximizing space and infrastructure efficiency, reducing the cost per megawatt of deployed compute, and making it easier to scale AI capacity within the same building—an increasingly critical advantage as demand for AI compute accelerates.
—-
Rack density measures the amount of power consumed by the equipment installed in a single rack, typically expressed in kW. A rack is the metal frame that holds servers, GPUs, networking gear, and other hardware inside a data center. Higher rack density means more power—and therefore more compute capability—packed into the same physical footprint, which impacts how much cooling, power delivery, and structural support the facility must provide. In 2023, the average data center rack density was 6 kW; in 2024, the average rack density was 12 kW (see blog.enconnex.com/data-cente… ). Less than 10% of data centers currently use immersion cooling ( jll.com/en-us/insights/data-… ). I interpret JLL Research’s graph as alleging that air cooling is only efficient for cooling up to a rack density of 25 kW, which is consistent with other sources.

NVIDIA’s HGX platforms—HGX 100 (based on the H100 GPU), HGX 200 (based on the H200 GPU), and HGX B200 (based on the B200 GPU)—are examples of hardware that drive high rack densities. Each HGX server contains eight GPUs and consumes significant power: around 10–12 kW for HGX 100, 12–13 kW for HGX 200, and 14–15 kW for HGX B200. When multiple servers are installed into racks, the total rack density typically ranges from about 30 kW to 60 kW, depending on how many systems fit into each rack.

Both a 15 kW rack and a 70–80 kW rack can technically run HGX B200 servers, but there are major differences in efficiency, cost, and practicality. At 15 kW rack density, only one HGX B200 server (or maybe two if you push limits) can fit into a single rack before hitting the power cap. This wastes a lot of physical space because racks are tall (typically 42–48U), but only a small portion of the available height is being used. Cooling and networking resources are being wasted because the infrastructure (e.g., airflow paths, cables, and switch ports) is designed to serve a fully populated rack, not just a half-empty one. In short, low rack density leads to underutilizing physical space and overpaying for space, cooling, and support systems. But increasing rack density is not trivial, which is why 37% of data centers still have racks of less than 10kW ( see blog.enconnex.com/data-cente… ).

At 70–80 kW rack density, it is possible to fully populate a rack with four to five HGX B200 servers. This configuration delivers significantly more compute power within the same physical footprint. The cost per megawatt of deployed compute declines substantially because each square foot, cooling system, and switch port is utilized more efficiently. Scaling also becomes simpler, as adding additional GPUs requires only the installation of another dense rack, rather than expanding floor space, power delivery, and cooling infrastructure.

The benefits of high rack density compound over time. A data center designed for 15 kW racks may quickly exhaust its available space and require costly expansions to accommodate additional GPUs. In contrast, a high-density facility can host two to four times as many GPUs within the same building. As a result, power and cooling costs per GPU are lower, and overall operational efficiency is significantly higher. While both low- and high-density facilities can technically support HGX B200 servers, high rack density enables a greater number of GPUs to be deployed per square foot at a lower total cost, which is critical as demand for AI compute continues to accelerate.

GPU CLUSTERING
TLDR:Iren’s high-density racks enable faster, more reliable communication with fewer switches and cables, improving cluster performance, reducing operational complexity, and lowering costs. High-density clustering unlocks the full performance of the hardware, while low-density setups limit efficiency, making dense GPU clustering increasingly critical as AI models grow larger and more complex.
—-
Eiso Kant, CTO and Co-Founder of poolside, commented: “We’ve been very impressed with the outperformance of IREN’s NVIDIA H100 GPU cluster as it sits amongst the best-in-class in reliability and performance, as well as the IREN team’s commitment to customer support. Our business has growing demand for GPU compute and we’re pleased to expand our partnership with IREN to support our growth.”

Clustering GPUs is critical for large-scale AI and high-performance computing (HPC) because modern workloads demand thousands of GPUs working together seamlessly. Large AI models like LLMs, recommendation engines, and scientific simulations require vast amounts of parallel computation. Clustering enables this by allowing GPUs to split workloads efficiently, communicate rapidly through high-bandwidth interconnects like NVLink and InfiniBand, and scale up to meet increasing computational demands. Without strong clustering, GPUs would struggle to synchronize, causing massive slowdowns, inefficiencies, and, in some cases, failures to complete the workload.

When clustering HGX B200 servers at a rack density of 30 kW, the process becomes significantly more difficult. Each HGX B200 system consumes about 10–15 kW, meaning only one or two can fit into a single rack. As a result, GPUs are physically spread across many racks, forcing longer cable runs and increasing the number of InfiniBand switches needed to wire them together. This added distance introduces latency, degrades communication speeds, and raises costs. The complexity of managing more switches, cables, and failure points makes it harder to maintain the cluster. Overall, clustering HGX B200s at 30 kW results in slower GPU-to-GPU communication and reduced scaling efficiency, hurting performance for large AI models that require tight synchronization.

In contrast, clustering HGX B200s at 80 kW rack density is much easier and far more efficient. At 80 kW, four to five HGX B200 servers can fit into a single rack, packing 32 to 40 GPUs closely together. Shorter physical distances between servers allow for faster, more reliable connections with fewer switches and cables. The entire cluster becomes simpler to build, cheaper to operate, and faster to scale. GPUs can communicate at high speeds with minimal latency, which dramatically improves model training times and overall cluster reliability. In high-density environments, operational overhead is lower, and the cluster can handle larger models and more complex workloads much more effectively.

Ultimately, clustering HGX B200s at 80 kW rack density unlocks the full potential of the hardware, while trying to cluster them at 30 kW significantly limits performance, increases cost, and complicates operations. As AI models continue to grow in size and complexity, the ability to densely cluster GPUs will become even more important for maintaining competitive advantage in AI and HPC markets.

text:
You are half right. And the half you are missing is worth billions.

Every generation has a moment where the 'middleware' looks doomed.

In 1994, everyone said ISPs were dead on arrival — why pay for internet access when the infrastructure would commoditize? Then AOL hit 30 million subscribers and sold for $164 billion.

In 2008, everyone said payment processors were toast — open banking would kill the middleman. Stripe was founded anyway. Now it's worth $65 billion.

The pattern isn't 'services die.' It's 'bad services die. Trusted services become infrastructure.'

Here's what the 'agents will rebuild everything cheaper' thesis misses:

Agents still need *trust rails.*

Stripe isn't valuable because it moves money. It's valuable because 10 million businesses trust it won't break on Black Friday. Vercel isn't valuable because it deploys code. It's valuable because it doesn't go down when your product goes viral at 2am.

AI can reprice capability. It cannot reprice *reliability reputation* built over a decade.

The companies that survive this aren't the ones with the best features. They're the ones that became the *default answer* when something absolutely cannot fail.

Commodity is a cost question. Trust is a different market entirely.

The graveyard of tech is full of cheaper alternatives that nobody used.

text:
US farmers are rejecting multimillion-dollar datacenter bids for their land: ‘I’m not for sale’ | Niamh Rowe, The Guardian

When two men knocked on Ida Huddleston’s door last May, they carried a contract worth more than $33m in exchange for the Kentucky farm that had fed her family for centuries.

According to Huddleston, the men’s client, an unnamed “Fortune 100 company”, sought her 650 acres (260 hectares) in Mason county for an unspecified industrial development. Finding out any more would require signing a non-disclosure agreement.

More than a dozen of her neighbors received the same knock. Searching public records for answers, they discovered that a new customer had applied for a 2.2 gigawatt project from the local power plant, nearly double its annual generation capacity.

The unknown company was building a datacenter.

“You don’t have enough to buy me out. I’m not for sale. Leave me alone, I’m satisfied,” Huddleston, 82, later told the men.

As tech companies race to build the massive datacenters needed to power artificial intelligence across the US and the world, bids like the one for Huddleston’s land are appearing on rural doorsteps nationwide. Globally, 40,000 acres of powered land – real estate prepped for datacenter development – are projected to be needed for new projects over the next five years, double the amount currently in use.

Yet despite sums that often dwarf the land’s recent value, farmers are increasingly shutting the door. At least five of Huddleston’s neighbors gave similar categorical rejections, including one who was told he could name any price.

In Pennsylvania, a farmer rejected $15m in January for land he’d worked for 50 years. A Wisconsin farmer turned down $80m the same month. Other landowners have declined offers exceeding $120,000 per acre – prices unimaginable just a few years ago.

The rebuffs are a jarring reminder of AI’s physical bounds, and limits of the dollars behind the technology.

The new Gold Rush

Four generations of the Huddleston family have watched the world change from the same fields.

Ida’s grandfather was growing tobacco when the civil war erupted. Her father ploughed wheat through the first world war and the long attrition of the Great Depression. She and her five siblings grew up on beans, broccoli and potatoes pulled from soil once seared by dust bowl winds. No one in her family went to college – but by age 10, her children could already herd cattle across the same ground as their forebears.

“My whole entire life is nothing but the land. It’s provided me with anything and everything that I’ve needed for 82 years,” she says, speaking from the cabin her late husband built using local wood and rocks many decades ago.

Today, where residents see meandering creeks and open pastures, Silicon Valley executives see weak zoning protections, cheap power and abundant water.

Developers keep knocking because there are billions to be made. In northern Virginia last November, an investor paid $615m for less than 100 acres – property the seller had bought for just $57m four years prior. Days later, Amazon spent $700m on nearby farmland that had sold for a fraction of that price the year before. In Georgia, a local developer flipped land to Amazon for $270m after paying $4m for it 12 months earlier. For the middlemen scouting these deals, potential returns exceed 1,000%.

‘Name your price’

About 20 Mason county residents have reportedly been offered deals, with the datacenter project estimated to cover 2,000 acres.

After Dr Timothy Grosser, 75, rejected an $8m offer for his 250-acre farm – 3,500% more than he’d paid nearly four decades earlier – the developers came back with a new proposition: “Name your price.”

His answer: “There is none.”

Grosser lives, hunts and raises cattle on his land. Each Christmas, his family eats a turkey his grandson catches there. Alongside Huddleston and himself, Grosser estimates four landowners have refused to sell.

“All they’ve done all their life is farm grain, cattle, tobacco,” Grosser says. “To them, same as me, the money’s not worth giving up your lifestyle.”

For Huddleston’s daughter, Delsia Bare, 56, the connection runs deeper than skill sets. She remembers hoeing weeds from tobacco fields alongside her mother and grandmother, putting up hay through Kentucky summers. “There’s a bond with the land,” she says. “There’s no way to undo it. That’s family, that’s history.”

Beyond personal attachment, some farmers worry about broader consequences. The number of US farms has dropped more than 70% since 1935. Datacenters can strain power grids, drain local water supplies, contaminate soil and fragment wildlife habitat.

Bare puts it more bluntly: “You’re not going to grow a loaf of bread off of a datacenter.”

Not everyone is holding out; some Mason county farmers have agreed to sell if the project proceeds. “You can’t blame them,” Grosser acknowledges. “Giving them 10 million bucks for a farm?”

Those who refuse to sell say the utility company has warned it may invoke eminent domain – the government power to seize private property for public use. The threat isn’t empty: Dominion Energy used it against a Virginia farmer last April.

‘Sometimes-self-sacrificial stewardship’

The resistance reflects something economists struggle to quantify: the cultural weight of land stewardship. In his book Love for the Land, author Brooks Lamb describes how family farmers’ “sometimes-self-sacrificial stewardship” can lead to choices that defy financial logic, like refusing to consolidate into industrial operations.

“When told to ‘get big or get out’, these farmers choose neither,” he writes.

Maintaining the farm is viewed as a “birthright”, by many, says Mary Hendrickson, a professor of rural sociology at the University of Missouri. The responsibility to previous generations runs deep, sometimes dangerously so. During the 1980s’ farm crisis, when heavily indebted farmers faced bankruptcy and land loss, more than 900 male farmers in the midwest committed suicide.

“They’re somewhat irreversible,” Hendrickson says. “If you give the land over to them, it destroys what that land could be for agriculture.”

‘Keeping our people here’

Local officials in Mason county insist the datacenter would sustain future generations by bringing much-needed tax revenue and jobs, an argument being made in town halls across the country.

Mason’s population has shrunk by around 10% since 1980, largely due to the loss of manufacturing. Developers say the datacenter project would bring 1,000 construction jobs, although it may only create 50 full-time operational jobs.

In places like Loudoun county, Virginia – home to “Data Center Alley”, where about a fifth of the world’s internet traffic goes through – datacenter tax revenue nearly equals the county’s entire operating budget.

“We can continue to shrink – losing population, losing jobs and watching our young people leave for opportunities elsewhere – or we can chart a new course,” Tyler McHugh, Mason county’s industrial development director, said at a public hearing in December. “It’s about keeping our people here.”

What money can’t buy

As they offer multimillion-dollar deals, datacenter developers are not stealing Mason county land, yet some farmers feel a spiritual dispossession nonetheless.

A few months before the knock on her door last May, Delsia Bare lost most of her vision. Now she relies on sound to connect with the land: singing birds, the running creek. She fears a datacenter’s hum will drown out those connections, pushing the farm from physical reality into memory.

For now, she returns to what her family has relied on for generations. “The land, the land, the land,” as her mother puts it.

As AI promises to transcend corporeal fallibility, these standoffs reveal its very physical constraints – and Wall Street’s miscalculation of what some people value most. In the rolling hills of Mason county and farmland across America, that gap is measured not in dollars but in something harder to price: identity.

** betterbail.com ** is a concise, two-word .COM domain composed of the positive, universally understood adjective “better” and the highly relevant legal term “bail.” 
- **No hyphens or numbers:** This ensures clarity and professionalism.

- **Bail:** Refers to the legal mechanism that allows individuals accused of a crime to be released from custody pending trial, typically upon payment or guarantee. “Bail” is a billion-dollar industry in North America and well-understood across English-speaking markets.

Combined, “Better Bail” is a brandable, aspirational phrase that signals innovation and customer-centricity in an industry known for complexity and skepticism. It suggests a modern solution to an old problem—ideal for startups, reformers, service providers, and legal tech.

text:
TON Ecosystem Update: March 2025

March was all about steady progress and resilience. While the broader market took some hits, TON stayed on track, pushing forward with infrastructure upgrades and gaining momentum across DeFi, payments, gaming, and Telegram-native experiences.

Missed last month’s update? Catch up on what happened in January–February in our last Ecosystem Repo

Pavel Durov’s return sparked confidence in TON’s growth.

Top VCs now hold $400M+ in Toncoin.

90% validator upgrade adoption in under 48 hours.

DeFi TVL surged, @wallet added new features and currencies, and RedotPay enabled USDt-TON payments at 130M+ merchants.

Miomi Game drove 5% of TON transactions with its sustainable Play2Win model, while NFT marketplace Tonnel broke daily volume records.

Elon Musk’s Grok AI joins Telegram.

TON shared its 2024 Grants recap.

Ecosystem confidence deepens: Durov’s return, investor backing

Telegram founder Pavel Durov’s return signaled long-term alignment between TON and Telegram, centered on freedom, privacy, and ownership.

Durov is FREE!  #DigitalResistance  prevails.  nitter.poast.org/ton_society/stat… 

— TON Society ( @ton_society ) March 17, 2025

At the same time, top VCs now collectively hold over $400 million in Toncoin, much of it US-based, reinforcing institutional support and positioning TON for broader expansion into America.

Infrastructure upgrades

TON Core rolled out multiple updates in March:

The new Pending API lets users track blockchain operations pre-finalization.

TON Wallet now supports the full tech stack – Jettons, NFTs, TON DNS, and more.

TON Layer 2 Payment Network gained Jetton support and laid out its roadmap, including Atomic Swaps.

90% of validators upgraded to the latest version within two days, a clear signal of ecosystem cohesion.

DeFi picks up steam

Factorial, a lending protocol, nearly doubled its TVL to $29M and is exploring incentive models. TONCO surged to $7.9M TVL and added ZAP, a new feature that lets users add liquidity with just one token. FIVA, TON’s first yield tokenization protocol, launched and reached $1M within days.

On the trading side, bots are becoming a serious force. Blum activated 75,000 on-chain users through its bot and drove 13% of all TON on-chain transactions by early April.

“The next mass adoption from DeFi will come from community-driven copy trading.”

— Steve Yun, TON Foundation Board Member

Payments stepping up

 @wallet  added trading features and support for a broader range of tokens like ETH, DOGE, and XRP, making it a real alternative to centralized exchanges (CEXs). Wallet Earn is now permanent, and USDT rewards will be available soon.

TON Space also introduced fee payments using Telegram Stars, which can be purchased directly in TON Space or transferred from a user's Telegram account.

Meanwhile, RedotPay integrated USDt-TON for real-world spending through Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Alipay—usable at 130M+ merchants, including Amazon and Starbucks. A Telegram Mini App is next.

GameFi and NFTs hit new highs

Telegram mini games saw massive adoption in March: Dropee hit 3.2M MAU, DUCK × MY × DUCK reached 1.2M, and Miomi Game accounted for 5% of all TON transactions in early March.

Telegram’s asset economy also experienced a successful month: Username @cryptoholder was sold for 250K TON, and Tonnel broke volume and trader records with 217K TON in volume and 5,806 unique traders.

Unlocking AI on TON

The groundwork is being laid for AI apps inside Telegram. Elon Musk’s Grok chatbot is now live, and TON x ElizaOS’s AI bounty program is boosting developer contributions.

grok now available directly on  @telegram 

— Grok ( @grok ) March 26, 2025

Wrapping up

March was all about building with intent. Institutional trust is rising, Telegram integrations are deepening, and builders are shipping everything from DeFi to NFTs to AI.

More updates are coming next month, including a deeper dive into TON Foundation’s 2025 roadmap

---

**Domain:** Solidity.ai 

---

**Character Count Analysis** 
- Characters before the dot (“.”): S, o, l, i, d, i, t, y = **8 characters**
- Characters after the dot (“.”): a, i = **2 characters**
- **Total character count:** 8 + 2 = **10 characters**

---

**Domain Construction & Content Evaluation** 
“ Solidity.ai ” is composed of the single English word “solidity” (8 characters) and the increasingly prestigious “.ai” extension (2 characters), for a total of 10 characters. The word “solidity” is clear, unambiguous, and easy to spell and pronounce. It passes the crucial “radio test” due to its recognizable pronunciation and widespread usage in English.

However, what truly amplifies the value of this domain is its direct reference to the popular programming language “Solidity,” which is the backbone for smart contracts and decentralized applications (dApps) on the Ethereum blockchain. “Solidity” is a technical term instantly recognized by blockchain developers, cryptocurrency enthusiasts, and anyone involved in decentralized finance (DeFi) and Web3 projects. This makes the domain hyper-relevant, highly brandable, and a natural fit for organizations, platforms, or tools working with Ethereum or smart contract development in combination with artificial intelligence.

---

**Top Level Domain (TLD) Analysis:** 
The “.ai” extension, originally the country code for Anguilla, has become the internationally recognized TLD for artificial intelligence. In today’s digital landscape, .ai domains are sought after by startups, enterprise AI solutions, and research communities. The explosive growth of AI, now intersecting with blockchain and smart contracts, means that .ai domains with strong, industry-specific keywords are in extreme demand.

While .COM remains the ultimate gold standard for global reach and credibility, .ai has become the unquestioned category leader for AI-centric businesses, research, and products. The synergy between the domain keyword (“Solidity”) and the .ai extension further increases its prestige and value.

---

**Acronym, Homonym, and Dual Meaning Analysis:** 
- **Acronym:** “Solidity” is not an acronym but a direct reference to the programming language and the concept of being solid or robust, both useful in branding.
- **Dual Meaning:** 
 - As a common English word, “solidity” conveys strength, reliability, and dependability—desired traits for any technology product.
 - As a technical term, “Solidity” is the official language for Ethereum smart contracts, and is the subject of countless tutorials, job listings, business solutions, and developer tools.
- **No Confusing Homonyms:** The term is familiar and its spelling is unique, reducing the potential for confusion.

---

**Line of Commerce Evaluation:** 
“ Solidity.ai ” sits at the crossroads of two of the most dynamic and rapidly expanding sectors: blockchain development (specifically Ethereum smart contracts) and artificial intelligence. This opens up several lucrative use cases:
- **AI Tools for Smart Contract Development:** The domain could be the flagship for a company or platform building AI-based tools to write, audit, or optimize Solidity code.
- **Blockchain Security:** Launch a security auditing firm employing machine learning to detect vulnerabilities in Solidity smart contracts.
- **Education:** Serve as a learning portal for AI-powered Solidity tutorials, developer bootcamps, or online courses.
- **Automated Testing/Deployment:** Offer cloud-based AI services for testing, deployment, or optimization of Solidity-based dApps.
- **Recruiting/Marketplace:** Become a marketplace for hiring Solidity developers or AI experts in blockchain.

Given the massive growth in DeFi, NFTs, and Web3 applications, and the increasing intersection with AI for code analysis, optimization, and autonomous systems, “ Solidity.ai ” is positioned at the heart of a multi-billion-dollar market with global reach.

---

text:
🚛 Will AI Be the Final Boss That Finally Kills the Freight Broker?

Let me take you back to 1989.

I'm sitting in a freight broker training program and the owner looks at us and says, "This new thing called the internet is going to replace freight brokers and change everything."

And I believed him. I had just booked my first airline ticket without a travel agent using a platform called EasySabre. It seemed like the writing was on the wall.

That was over 30 years ago.

The freight broker industry didn't die. It exploded.

Then came Uber. Everyone swore Uber would transform freight the same way it transformed transportation. It didn't.

Then came Convoy — backed by Jeff Bezos, Bill Gates, and over a BILLION dollars in venture capital. They were going to automate the broker out of existence. In 2022 they were valued at $3.8 BILLION.

In 2023 they sold for $16 million.

Pennies. On. The. Dollar.

Now Wall Street is in a panic over AI. Landstar, C.H. Robinson, RXO — stocks tanked on fears that AI is coming for the broker's lunch. Again.

So here's my question for you:

👉 Is AI actually the Final Boss that takes down the freight brokerage industry — or is this just the same movie with a different title?

I've always said moving freight is fundamentally different from moving people. Freight doesn't have a destination preference. Freight doesn't tip. Freight doesn't cancel at 2am because it found a cheaper option. Freight is relationships, trust, liability, and complexity stacked on top of each other — 80,000 lbs at a time.

Every generation of tech has promised to automate the human out of this equation.

Every generation has been wrong.

Maybe AI is different. Maybe this time the disruption is real.

Or maybe we're about to watch another billion-dollar tech bet get humbled by the reality of moving iron down the highway.

What do you think? Drop it in the comments. 👇

text:
What Are Web3 Domains?

Web3 domains are decentralized domain names built on blockchain technology, often tied to protocols like Ethereum Name Service (ENS), Handshake (HNS), or Unstoppable Domains. Unlike traditional domains (e.g., .com or .org) managed by centralized entities like ICANN, Web3 domains are:

Decentralized: Stored on a blockchain, not controlled by a single authority.

Immutable: Once registered, ownership is cryptographically secured.

Multifunctional: Can serve as domain names, cryptocurrency wallet addresses, identity markers, or access points to decentralized websites.

Censorship-resistant: Harder to seize or shut down compared to traditional domains.
Examples include .eth (ENS), .crypto, or .nft domains. These domains are often marketed as the foundation for a decentralized internet, aligning with the broader Web3 vision of user-owned, blockchain-based ecosystems.
Why Web3 Domains Can Be a Good Investment
1. Early Adoption in a Growing Ecosystem

Context: Web3 represents the next evolution of the internet, emphasizing decentralization, user sovereignty, and blockchain integration. As of 2025, Web3 adoption is still in its early stages, with growing interest in decentralized applications (dApps), NFTs, DAOs, and the metaverse.

Investment Angle: Buying Web3 domains now is akin to investing in .com domains during the early internet era (1990s). Early adopters who secured valuable .com names (e.g., business.com , sold for $7.5M in 1999) reaped massive profits as the internet grew. Similarly, Web3 domains tied to popular keywords, brands, or concepts could appreciate significantly if Web3 becomes mainstream.

Example: A domain like “crypto.eth” or “nft.eth” could become highly valuable if Ethereum-based ecosystems dominate Web3, as these names are short, memorable, and relevant.
2. Scarcity and Speculative Value

Context: Many Web3 domain systems, like ENS, have a finite namespace for certain extensions (e.g., .eth). Once a domain is registered, it’s locked to the owner unless sold or relinquished. This scarcity mimics real estate, where prime “locations” (short, memorable names) are limited.

Investment Angle: High-demand domains (e.g., single-word names like “love.eth” or “game.eth”) are already commanding premium prices in secondary markets. For instance, ENS domains have sold for thousands to millions of dollars (e.g., “paradigm.eth” sold for $1.5M in 2021). Investors can buy low now and sell high later as demand grows.

Market Trend: Data from platforms like OpenSea shows consistent trading volume for ENS domains, with rare names fetching six-figure sums in ETH. This speculative fervor mirrors early domain flipping but is amplified by blockchain’s global, permissionless nature.
3. Utility Beyond Traditional Domains
Context: Web3 domains aren’t just URLs; they have versatile use cases:
Wallet Addresses: Domains like “yourname.eth” can simplify crypto transactions by replacing long wallet addresses (e.g., 0x1234…).
Decentralized Websites: They can host content on IPFS or other decentralized networks, bypassing traditional hosting.
Digital Identity: They act as cross-platform identifiers for Web3 profiles, NFTs, or metaverse avatars.
Smart Contract Integration: Domains can be programmed for governance, payments, or access control in DAOs.

Investment Angle: This multifunctionality increases their value proposition. As Web3 ecosystems grow (e.g., Ethereum, Solana, or Polkadot), domains tied to these networks could become essential infrastructure, driving demand. Businesses or individuals may pay premiums for domains that streamline their Web3 presence.

Example: A brand like Nike could buy “nike.eth” to unify its crypto wallet, NFT marketplace, and decentralized site, making it a valuable asset.

4. Branding and Marketing Opportunities

Context: In Web3, branding is critical as projects compete for attention in a crowded space. A memorable domain can signal credibility, innovation, and alignment with decentralized values.

Investment Angle: Companies, influencers, or DAOs may seek Web3 domains to establish a strong digital presence. Investors can acquire domains aligned with trending niches (e.g., “defi.eth” for decentralized finance or “vr.crypto” for virtual reality) and sell them to relevant players. This mirrors traditional domain squatting but with a Web3 twist.

Trend: Major brands are already experimenting with Web3. For example, Budweiser purchased “beer.eth” in 2021 for $95K, signaling corporate interest in Web3 branding.
5. Global Accessibility and Ownership

Context: Web3 domains are accessible to anyone with a crypto wallet, bypassing geographic or regulatory barriers. Ownership is absolute (as long as you hold the private key), unlike traditional domains, which require annual renewals and can be seized.

Investment Angle: This global market increases liquidity and demand, as buyers from anywhere can participate in auctions or secondary markets. The permanence of ownership also appeals to long-term holders who want to “HODL” valuable domains without ongoing costs (in some systems, like Unstoppable Domains, no renewals are needed).

Example: A domain like “freedom.crypto” could appeal to a global audience advocating for decentralization, driving its resale value.
6. Network Effects and Platform Adoption

Context: The value of Web3 domains is tied to the success of their underlying platforms. For instance, ENS domains gain utility as more dApps integrate .eth for payments, identity, or access. Similarly, Handshake domains could soar if its vision of a decentralized DNS replaces ICANN.

Investment Angle: Investing in domains on established or promising blockchains (e.g., Ethereum, Solana) leverages network effects. As these ecosystems grow, their domains become more entrenched, increasing in value. For example, ENS has over 800K registered names as of 2023, with integrations in wallets like MetaMask and exchanges like Coinbase.

Trend: Partnerships, like ENS’s integration with GoDaddy in 2024 to bridge Web2 and Web3, suggest growing mainstream acceptance, which could boost domain values.
7. Speculative Hype and Cultural Relevance

Context: Web3 is driven by community enthusiasm, memes, and cultural trends. Domains tied to hot topics (e.g., “ai.eth” for artificial intelligence or “meme.crypto” for meme coins) can ride waves of hype.

Investment Angle: Speculators can capitalize on short-term flips by buying domains aligned with trending narratives. For instance, during the 2021 NFT boom, domains like “nft.eth” surged in value. Investors with foresight into cultural shifts (e.g., metaverse, AI, or gaming) can acquire relevant domains early.

Example: The domain “420.eth” sold for $400K in 2022, driven by cannabis culture and crypto’s meme-driven market.
Risks and Considerations

While Web3 domains have strong investment potential, they come with risks that must be weighed:

Speculative Nature: Much of the value is driven by hype, and prices can crash if interest wanes or Web3 fails to scale.

Platform Risk: A domain’s value is tied to its blockchain (e.g., ENS relies on Ethereum). If the platform loses relevance, so do its domains.
Regulatory Uncertainty: Governments may crack down on decentralized systems, affecting domain utility or legality.
Market Saturation: As more domain extensions emerge (e.g., .sol, .bnb), competition could dilute value.

Technical Barriers: Mainstream adoption requires user-friendly interfaces, which are still developing. If Web3 remains niche, demand may stall.

Liquidity Risk: Selling a domain requires finding a buyer, which can be challenging for obscure names.

Strategies for Investing in Web3 Domains

To maximize returns, consider these approaches:

Focus on Premium Names: Short, memorable, or keyword-rich domains (e.g., “art.eth,” “shop.crypto”) have broader appeal.

Research Trends: Target niches with growth potential, like AI, gaming, or DeFi. Follow X posts or Web3 news for real-time insights.
Diversify Across Platforms: Invest in domains on multiple blockchains (e.g., ENS, Unstoppable, Handshake) to hedge against platform-specific risks.
Engage in Flipping or Holding: Flip trending domains for quick profits or hold valuable ones for long-term appreciation.

Monitor Secondary Markets: Platforms like OpenSea, Namebase, or ENS Vision track domain sales, helping you gauge demand and pricing.

Real-World Examples and Data

ENS Sales: Per OpenSea and ENS Vision, top ENS domains like “000.eth” (sold for 300 ETH, ~$1M in 2022) and “win.eth” (100 ETH, ~$300K) show strong market activity.

Market Growth: ENS reported 2.2M name registrations by 2023, with $100M+ in secondary market trades. Unstoppable Domains crossed 3M registrations in 2024.

Corporate Adoption: Brands like Puma (“puma.eth”) and Coinbase (integrating .eth wallets) signal institutional interest, boosting domain credibility.
Web3 Trends: Posts on X highlight rising interest in Web3 identity and metaverse domains, with users speculating on names like “meta.eth” or “vr.crypto.”

Conclusion

Buying Web3 domains can be a compelling investment due to their scarcity, multifunctionality, and alignment with the growing Web3 ecosystem. Early adopters stand to benefit from speculative hype, branding opportunities, and potential mainstream adoption, much like early .com investors. However, the market is highly speculative, with risks tied to platform success, regulatory shifts, and market volatility. By focusing on premium names, staying informed on trends, and diversifying, investors can position themselves for significant returns while managing risks.

text:
My co-founder Miguel Salis and I built Eolia Renovables, a company focused on large-scale solar and wind farms that we sold for €1.1bn, followed by Barter Energy, which pioneered solar rooftop communities. While we successfully exited both ventures—Barter Energy just yesterday—I’ve grown deeply critical of the renewable energy paradigm. My perspective stems not from ideology but from firsthand experience and reflection on the unintended consequences of our work.

The apocalyptic climate projections of the early 2000s, which drove much of the renewable push, caused significant psychological harm, instilling fear in millions. These predictions—often overstated—have largely failed to materialize. Yes, CO2 emissions have contributed to more frequent extreme weather, but the scale of the threat has been exaggerated. Today, extreme weather claims roughly 60,000 lives annually worldwide, a tragic but relatively small number compared to the 1 million deaths from car accidents. Yet, policies rooted in climate alarmism have justified impoverishing citizens, particularly in Europe and Spain, where energy costs have soared, doubling those in the U.S. High energy prices breed poverty, erode industrial competitiveness, and leave nations unprepared for the energy demands of transformative technologies like AI.

I now believe large-scale solar and wind, as pursued by Eolia Renovables, were a mistake. These projects razed forests, destroyed beautiful landscapes, and uprooted centenarian olive trees—environmental devastation in the name of "green" energy. The result? An inefficient, intermittent energy system dependent on massive government subsidies, prone to blackouts, and incapable of meeting modern energy needs. Europe’s energy policies have prioritized ideology over pragmatism, with Germany’s “energy suicide” serving as a stark warning: its industrial base now teeters on collapse due to unreliable and costly energy.

I’ve shifted my support to new nuclear energy, which is clean, reliable, and environmentally benign. Unlike wind and solar farms, nuclear doesn’t require sprawling land use or ecosystem disruption. It’s the backbone we need for a stable, affordable, and sustainable energy future. The only renewable I still endorse is rooftop solar paired with battery storage, like the Elon Musk vision of Tesla Powerwall, solar roofs, and electric vehicles. Rooftop solar minimizes environmental impact—using existing structures—and enables localized energy production and consumption. It’s a practical solution that reduces reliance on fossil fuels and cuts air pollution, which kills 100 times more people than extreme weather.

My skepticism of climate alarmism is rooted in history. In the 1970s, the Club of Rome’s report predicted global starvation by 2000—a terrifying falsehood debunked by advances in agricultural technology. Today’s climate narrative feels eerily similar. The 1.5°C of warming we’ve seen is manageable—Washington, D.C., is 1.5°C warmer than New York City, yet both thrive. Dire predictions, like Madrid turning into the Sahara, clash with reality: Spain is experiencing its wettest spring on record in 2025. Miami’s hurricane risk remains unchanged from the 1980s. These discrepancies expose the limits of long-term climate modeling. If we can’t predict next year’s weather with precision, how can we trust forecasts decades out?

Fossil fuels—coal, gas, and oil—should be phased out thoughtfully to reduce emissions, but not at the expense of economic stability. Europe’s rush to renewables without a viable backup has crippled its economies. We must prioritize energy policies that balance environmental goals with affordability and reliability. Nuclear and rooftop solar offer a path forward; dogmatic renewables and fear-driven policies do not. Let’s learn from Germany’s mistakes and build an energy future that powers progress without sacrificing prosperity

4 | Saw little impact from tariffs thus far, continue to monitor

Yes, I'll take the tariffs. I mean, I would say it's still early to kind of be able to judge specifically. I would say we don't have much direct exposure to it. But ultimately, anything that impacts our clients does impact us. It's just -- we haven't seen anything yet. And -- but it is something that we'll continue to monitor. I would say that it would have to have an impact on employee count and the overall employment, I would say, to really have a meaningful impact on us. But like everyone else, it's something we're monitoring.

5 | Not seeing any changes to demand

Yes. I mean, the mid-market opportunity, I mean, I would say everywhere for us is going very well. I mean, we're not seeing any changes to demand. If anything, I've always kind of said we also create demand ourselves by the work we do. 6 | GONE’s automated time-off solution is helping organisations save time, reducing errors, lower costs and staffing shortages

We have the most automated solution in the industry and our clients routinely attested this. Our award-winning solution, GONE, is a perfect example of how Paycom simplifies tests through automation and AI. GONE is the industry's first fully automated time-o solution that decisions all time-off requests based on customizable guidelines set by the company's time-off rules. This honor speci cally recognized GONE and is a testament to how Paycom is shaping our industry by setting new standards for automation across the globe.

7 | BETI continues to help clients process payrolls faster and cut time on errors

Another example of automation that is changing our industry is Beti. Our award-winning payroll solution continues to be a major selling point. Organizations looking to reduce the labor needed to process payroll by up to 90% and also cut the time spent correcting payroll errors by up to 85%. Beti allows clients to focus resources on profit-driving initiatives as it eliminates human involvement in non-revenue-generating tasks like post payroll adjustments, check reversals, voids, ledger corrections and more.

8 | BETI helped to bring back a client that left, and went back to PAYC in 4 hours versus 4 days for the previous vendor

Thanks to Beti and the importance of perfect payrolls, we are also successfully getting former clients back onto the Paycom platform. We recently brought back a 500 employee health care company, who quickly realized the pain they brought on themselves by switching to another provider. With this other provider, this client lost the transparency and ability to x errors before they became problems. In fact, their employees were some of the biggest advocates and encourage this client to return to Paycom because they missed having control over the accuracy of their pay. Once employees experience Beti, they don't want to go backwards in technology. The client returned to us within 9 months and went from processing payroll in 4 days with their previous vendor to 4 hours with Beti.

9 | Focused on getting clients back

We're also focused on that. We want every client to come back. I mean, there's no questions asked on our part, let's get going. And so we do have a strategy to get clients that have left back. We also have a strategy to make sure that clients are receiving the value so that they don't have to go through that pain of a conversion to just to turn around and come back to us. And so that remains a part of our overall strategy. It has, and we're having a lot of success with that.

10 | Raised FY25 guide slightly

Now let me turn to guidance for 2025. We continue to have success selling and onboarding new logos. Based on our strong Q1 results and outlook for the remainder of the year, we are raising our full year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance ranges.

11 | Authorization as payment institution from Central Bank of Ireland allows Paycom to move money throughout Europe

So Ireland and being there allows us to get to the rest of Europe from there. And we've been focused on continuing to build out our product. I mentioned global HCM that works for all countries. We continue to onboard for that. We actually process native payroll in for other countries other than the U.S., which includes the banking side of it. And so we're continuing to do that. And this was one of the steps that you take to be able to continue to move further into Europe

This allows us to move money throughout Europe. The last yard of a payroll is actually getting it into the employee's account correctly. And if you do everything else right, you don't do that part, you kind of did nothing. So for us to make sure that we ensure the highest quality for all of our clients, we like to keep the ball in our hand, and this is something that's required to do that.

12 | Re-ramping up sales, seeing positive traction

Yes. So well, first on the sell side, I would say that we've been continuing to get better and better in sales. I do believe that our sales sta is the best in the world at what they do. And we did have a reconstitution, if you will, of training early part of last year, as Amy kind of took over the group to get back to the normal blocking and tackling that we've always done here at Paycom. That resulted in increased sales, especially as well as increased units, new logo adds. Obviously, those came on throughout the year and most would have all started by now. And then as we turned into first quarter, we saw a continuation of the same, up meaningfully in both book sales and units. And so activity matters in sales.

There are several tasks that we have to perform on the back end that we've been able to automate, and that has an impact on our adjusted EBITDA across the board, but it also has an impact on the client experience. And that's really why we're doing a lot of the things that we're doing through automation. I'd like to say the only reason a client even calls us is due to the deficiency in the software that we create. And so that's been impacting our margins, and that's been impacting our sales.

14 | Remain focused on creating value from automation

And so we're that type of business, we create value for our clients when we automate, we create value for ourselves when we automate, and that's what we've been focused on for quite some time now, and it's rolling out. text:
How to exit from any narrative in time? 

In most cases, when you lose money, it's due to the narrative no longer being relevant at the moment

This shift can happen very quickly, and you might not even notice it

That's why I’ve made a checklist with potential triggers

I’ll show how it works using NFTs as an example, and the main factors you could’ve paid attention to

But you can use a similar checklist for:

- AI-tokens
- RWA
- GameFi
- Memecoins
- Other trends

------

> [ CHECKLIST: “How to exit a narrative without losing everything?” ]

1. Trading Volume

After euphoria and a vertical rise without corrections, the end usually comes

At least, that’s what happened with NFTs

OpenSea hit $3.5B in January 2022, then dropped below $430M by mid-2023 (-88%)

Now volume is $10–25M a day (–99% from ATH)

2. Unique Buyers

If buyers outnumber sellers, this shows retail interest and new ATHs being made

But if sellers outnumber buyers for several weeks or more, this can lead to a full-on drop

It's important to research these factor at the moment to make timely decisions

In January 2022, the NFT sector had 1.04M buyers (CryptoSlam stats)

But now it’s down to 28.6k buyers (–97%)

3. Search / Social Interest

Social interest means direct interest and people searching specific terms online

You can track this with Google Trends and evaluate using a scoring scale

Bullish: Google Trends score above 50, ideally 70–100

If it drops below 30, then below 20, that’s a bearish factor

For example, the word "NFT" had a peak Google Trends score of ~100 in 2021

Now it ranges from 3 to 20 , interest has dumped

Same trend with the word “memecoin”: ATH in Dec 2024 – Jan 2025

Now the GT score is around 15–20...

4. Partnerships and Celebrities

Harder to track with data, but: after celebrities and their collections entered NFTs, volumes peaked and then started to dump

If you analyze it, the market downturn also started after Trump’s memecoin, that shows celebrity influence

These are real tops, when mainstream (Web2) interest is near all-time highs in most cases

That’s the moment when, as a Web3 user, you should already be locking in profits

5. Blue-Chip Floor Prices

A bullish factor: blue-chips setting new ATHs compared to the previous cycle

But if most of them start falling by 50–90%, while smaller collections are still afloat, it’s a red flag

Time to dig deeper and do more analysis

Many Solana collections, for example, could still be sold for a good price even in a bear market

Just as an example, one of the most popular collections BAYC:

Floor price was 153.7 ETH → now it's 10–15 ETH (–93%)

Same thing happened with most memecoins:

When blue-chips dropped 30–40%, they later continued to fall to - 80-90%

-----------

> [ CONCLUSION ]

Exit checklist from a narrative (DYOR, NFA):

1. Unique buyers < 20% of the cycle peak

→ Track via CryptoSlam “Global Sales Volume”

2. Blue-chip floors break below last cycle’s consolidation range

→ Track via NFTpriceFloor or other aggregators for other narratives

3. Google Trends score < 20 while 30-day volume keeps falling

→ Use trends.google.com and enter the keyword

4. Volume dumped sharply by 50–80%+

→ Track via any aggregator: Dexscreener or CryptoRank (always DYOR)

→ You can also use Dune and set up Dune alerts

5. If all metrics show bearish signals, and FUD is spreading on socials

→ Watch for sentiment shifts, how founders respond, and overall audience reaction

If volume, unique buyers, views, and general interest are falling, it’s time to think

text:
🙏 Thank You God, Family, and Friends 🙏

MyVehicle .com Sold for $105,000 via @Escrow_com 

Every journey has milestones that leave a lasting impression on our hearts. For me, MyVehicle .com will always hold a special place in my entrepreneurial story — not just for its value, but for the journey, faith, and patience it demanded.

I’m happy to share that MyVehicle .com has officially been sold for $105,000 via @Escrow_com , concluding a 60-month lease-to-own deal that began with a heartfelt negotiation and just wrapped up successfully. The negotiation took about 6 months, but the full payout and relationship spanned over 5 years.

We always remember our first range-breaker — that defining deal which resets what we once thought was possible. The automotive sector has played a huge role in my life. In fact, ElectricCar .com, which I sold for $180,000, was my first single-payment six-figure deal. But MyVehicle .com holds the title for my first agreed six-figure deal, structured over a long-term plan — and now completed in full.

The Backstory

I acquired MyVehicle .com back in 2018 via a NameJet auction. Around that time, I already owned ElectricCar .com, and my vision was clear: collect premium automotive assets that could define the future, especially as EV (Electric Vehicle) interest was just starting to surge.

MyVehicle .com stood out to me as a powerful umbrella term — versatile and broad, applicable across multiple facets of the auto industry. Over the years, I consistently received serious inquiries. In 2019, one interested party started with a $5,000 offer, which through discussion reached $25,000 — a fantastic ROI considering I had only held it for under a year. But I politely declined while keeping the door open, as I had long-term conviction that the name would eventually break the six-figure mark, even if some found that laughable back then.

The Deal That Tested Patience and Character

In February 2020, just as COVID fears were beginning to spread, our daughter came down with a flu. My wife and I soon followed with similar symptoms. Doctors told us to rest — back then, no COVID testing was available, and we had no way of knowing what it really was.

Amidst that, I received an unexpected email — the same person who had offered $25,000 six months prior was back. I immediately recognized his name and revisited our past conversation. We got on a phone call, speaking for over an hour. I walked him through facts, market trends, and data — highlighting that even at the time, the highest known public sale with the keyword “Vehicle” was VehicleHistoryReport .com for $31,000.

The buyer appreciated the insight, but had budget constraints. I remembered wise advice once shared by @BradenPollock : "Always try your best to help your customer find a solution." So, instead of walking away, I offered a structured plan.

Initially, I asked for $15,000–$20,000 as down payment, with the balance in monthly installments. Since the buyer preferred using a credit card for his initial payments, I knew I couldn’t expect more than $5,000 per month due to processing limitations.

So, we worked out a custom plan:

Down Payment Schedule (First 4 Months)

Month 1: $4,735 ($2,300 + $2,434.50 escrow fees)

Month 2: $4,750

Month 3: $4,750

Month 4: $4,750

Installment Structure

Months 5–15: $1,580 per month

Months 16–27: $1,000 per month(adjusted due to COVID-related constraints)

Months 28–60: $1,790 per month

A Lesson in Patience and Faith

As the deal unfolded, there were numerous delays and inconsistencies in payments — some of which are clearly visible in our transaction screenshots. The buyer often reached out asking for understanding due to market uncertainty.

Many times, I could have enforced my rights. Per Escrow rules, I could have emailed them, and if no payment was made in 7 days, I could have reclaimed the asset and kept all payments made up to that point. But I chose not to.

Why?

Because I believe in God, ethics, morality, and trust — even when tested. God gave me several such tests during this period. I saw each moment as a choice to stand by my values rather than chase short-term gain. I believe in positive vibe deal. Hence I always supported all of his requests.

And I’m glad I did.

With God’s blessings, the buyer fully paid off the domain last month, marking the completion of my first-ever agreed six-figure lease-to-own deal.

A Bittersweet Twist

Just 5 months after this deal began, Vehicle .com hit the market. I had recently completed my ElectricCar .com sale and had fresh capital to reinvest. Naturally, I wanted to grab Vehicle .com to round off my portfolio. I offered $75,000, but it eventually sold to another investor for $120,000. I was genuinely happy for the buyer. I believe in celebrating others after they’ve executed.

Reflecting on the Journey

Today, six-figure deals are a regular part of my business, with God’s grace. I’m now averaging six figures in domain sales monthly, with a consistent five-figure income stream from active lease-to-own agreements.

Beyond domains, I’ve been receiving great returns in other investments as well — from real estate, crypto, stocks, mutual funds, gold, and bonds — all showing exceptional CAGR.

Each of these has a story, and I may share more from those experiences another time.

Final Thoughts

Warren Buffett once said, “Don’t put all your eggs in one basket,” while @elonmusk Elon Musk countered, “You can put all your eggs in one basket — just watch that basket closely.” I admire both, and I try to find a balanced path across various sectors.

Life will always bring challenges. What matters is how we respond — how we show up for the tests life throws at us. Those are the exams we must pass to graduate to the next level.

This was more than a domain sale. It was a story of patience, conviction, ethical conduct, and divine timing.

Thank you again to God, my family, and all friends who’ve supported me on this path.

🙏🙏🙏

Genuinely trading now is the worst it’s been for me, congratulations if you make money now.

Forever this game was about people buying and people selling - someone had to lose money in order for one to make it. Some coins though, were different. Even if you were early and sold for profit in first initial candles, that was just an entry for serious players that wanted to ride it to multimillions. 

I really liked how memecoins gave so many asymmetric bets if you were early to informations you’ve found. For example recently, moonpig was coin with low risk but huge upside if you bet for James Wynn. The attention he gathered was something else, yet his coin was only at 20-30M.

It is the same with ICM/2024 AI coins where you followed volume or DD’ed early, you could sell at 1-10M (with <500k entry) but the coins still went higher because sized players hoped for even more millions. That’s how both early players made money and how whales could size in for profit. 

Now, these plays seems to be gone, seriously. After the initial ICM hype, launchpad fights and everything else, current coins that run are nothing else than gamble (besides Labubu and few other viral coins that were underpriced for long time). Random BONK animals are just a gamble. Every other pump coin is.. well gamble. I’m risking 10 SOL at 200K for coin to go up and down and I don’t know where will it go, because all the information is there and unless Lexapro or other cabal buys - the coin goes to zero.

With ICM coins there was no insider advantage, just you and your fast DD skills. Yes this is semi-crashout post because I keep losing money but wonder, where does it end and when do we comeback to something worth buying?

text:
What is @NATIXNetwork ?

NATIX Network ( @NATIXNetwork ) is a blockchain-based, decentralized physical infrastructure network (DePIN) that leverages AI, edge computing, and smartphone cameras to create a real-time, crowdsourced geospatial intelligence network. Its flagship product, the "Drive&" app, allows users to earn rewards by collecting geospatial data using their smartphone cameras while driving, without needing additional hardware. The network aims to build a dynamic, privacy-focused map of the world to support applications like autonomous driving, smart city services, and advanced mapping.

📢Data Collection: AI analyzes video streams in real-time to detect events like traffic conditions, road obstacles, or parking availability, converting them into anonymous metadata to ensure privacy.

📢Data Validation: Decentralized techniques verify data accuracy and authenticity.

📢Data Monetization: A marketplace allows data to be sold for real-time applications, with contributors earning $NATIX tokens or iLand NFT royalties.

📢Tokenomics: The $NATIX token, built on the Solana blockchain, is used for rewards, staking, governance, and in-app utilities. The ecosystem also includes iLand NFTs, representing geographical tiles for passive income.

📢VX360 Device: A device for Tesla owners to monetize 360° dashcam and sentry footage, enhancing data collection for autonomous driving.

📢Founded in 2020 by NATIX GmbH in Hamburg, Germany, the network has grown rapidly, with over 200,000 registered drivers and 131 million kilometers mapped across 171 countries. It uses a deflationary token model to increase $NATIX value over time and has raised $13.1 million in funding. The platform emphasizes privacy, processing data locally on devices to avoid storing personal information.

Start staking here: staking.natix.network

text:
Sometimes I like to do an exercise in my head, where I try to predict where things are going with AI video. It helps orient myself and do a gut check on what I’m doing.

Here are some thoughts (some spicy🥵) that came to mind today.👇

------

I think there are a lot of AI video companies right now. There will come a point where the VC well runs dry and consolidation will happen.

Hollywood seems to be opening up slowly to AI as more top executives and talent start to talk positively about it.

In contrast, I think that people are overestimating the general public’s readiness for AI video.

I think AI video will need a “Jurassic Park” like moment to gain acceptance and desire for AI video by the general public.

The “Jurassic Park” moment will not be a movie, but a universe.

I think most AI video creators are thinking like Toyota, building a hybrid model like the Prius, trying to get the best of both worlds, trying to appease both sides of the controversy. To get the full benefits of AI, they will need to be like Tesla and go all-in on AI, just like Tesla went all-in on electric.

The best creators have a clear vision and are relentless and uncompromising in bringing their ideas to life. So the AI tools that give them exactly what they want will win and for better or for worse, it will not matter how they are made.

AI video is still in the skeuomorphic stage. Most are trying to make it look like something they already know, a movie, a video game, a music video. An extremely successful new form and aesthetic will be invented by an AI video creator and that will bring the medium into its own.

From listening to podcasts like “The Town”, it feels like comedians have found a great business outside of the Hollywood system through doing their own stand-up theater performances, podcasts, YouTube, etc. (listen to Mike Birbiglia’s interview on The Town”). I wonder if the first real breakout success of AI video will be comedy. Sci-fi is also a natural fit, but I feel that the general public has grown to have such a singular but still sophisticated taste for sci-fi that you need to rewrite the rules of the sci-fi genre to have a chance.

The “forgotten” NFT community (at least by main stream media who think it’s totally dead, just like how they thought chatbots were dead, then came along ChatGPT) is a hidden enclave of people who fully embrace AI and are spending good money to buy AI art (a Lost Robbie recently sold for $550K). I believe the NFT community is where to look to get a glimpse of the future of AI video both as an art form but also demand and business model.

I think AI video supply will be a major problem. There will be an immense supply of AI trash/slop, but also an extraordinarily small supply of quality AI video. This will make it extremely hard to find good AI videos and thus curators or “scouts” will potentially be a lucrative position that I think will come out of just being present and being in the community today. A very small number of the AI artists today will go on to be rockstars, the others will be friends of the rockstars and thus have access to them like very few will.

🤑 $15 Million for a Domain? The Unreal True Story of NFTs.com !

🌐 The Digital Real Estate Boom

In the world of domain names—where digital real estate is as valuable as physical property—the name NFTs.com was a crown jewel waiting for the perfect moment. That moment came in August 2022, during the peak of the NFT (Non-Fungible Token) frenzy. While most of the world was focused on monkey JPEGs and million-dollar digital art, behind the scenes, a major transaction was brewing.

🔥 The Sale That Turned Heads

In a private transaction, the domain NFTs.com was sold for a jaw-dropping $15 million in cash.

This made it one of the largest domain sales ever publicly reported, trailing just behind legendary sales like:

 Voice.com – $30 million (2019)
 Sex.com – $13 million (2010)
 Fund.com – $9.99 million (2008)

It was more expensive than Hotels.com , FB.com , and even PrivateJet.com —making NFTs.com not just a digital asset, but a statement of belief in the NFT future.

🧩 Who Sold and Who Bought It?

The deal was brokered by domain industry veterans, including:

 Domainer.com (a top-tier domain brokerage firm)

GoDaddy (the largest domain registrar in the world)

The identities of both the seller and buyer were kept confidential, but speculation quickly flooded the industry.

🔍 Speculated Buyer: Many believed the buyer was connected to the Web3 ecosystem, possibly affiliated with the digital artist platform DigitalArtists.com or entities behind prominent NFT projects.

A few weeks after the sale, NFTs.com began displaying a basic landing page with a connection to the NFT community and links to some NFT-related services—further fueling speculation.

💡 Why Was NFTs.com So Valuable?

Let’s break it down:

1. Exact Match & Category-Defining
 NFTs.com is the exact match keyword for the entire NFT industry. It’s like owning Cars.com in the auto industry or Hotels.com in the travel industry. It instantly gives the owner credibility, SEO dominance, and brand power.

2. Short & Memorable
Three characters. Dot com. Universal understanding. Even people outside of crypto recognize the term “NFTs” now.

3. Explosive Market
At the time of the sale, the NFT market had exploded into a multi-billion-dollar industry. Projects like Bored Ape Yacht Club, CryptoPunks, and marketplaces like OpenSea were making headlines daily.

4. Investment Value
Even if the buyer didn’t build anything on it, the resale potential of NFTs.com was massive. Many saw it as digital gold.

📈 The Impact on the Domain Industry

The sale of NFTs.com proved several things:

Premium domains are still extremely valuable, especially when tied to trending or emerging industries.

The domain market isn’t just for tech companies anymore—crypto and Web3 investors are starting to understand the power of owning the "digital front door" of an industry.

Brand trust, organic traffic, and investor attention all skyrocket when you own a name like NFTs.com .

🔮 What’s Next for NFTs.com ?

As of now, NFTs.com is still under quiet development, but all eyes are watching. It could become:

A massive NFT marketplace

A Web3 community hub

A high-traffic media and news site

Or even a brand asset for resale

Whatever it becomes, the sale of NFTs.com marks a milestone moment in both the domain and crypto industries.

🧠 Final Thought

If Voice.com was the domain sale that proved enterprise companies care about premium .com names, then NFTs.com proved that Web3 and crypto buyers do too. It’s a reminder that even in a decentralized future, the centralized power of a great domain name is still unmatched

Once upon a digital canvas, before NFT became a word that echoed through crypto halls, before digital art fetched millions, there was Mike Winkelmann, known as Beeple.

The world gasped. Digital art had arrived. Beeple was crowned king of NFTs.

A triumph?

Long before Beeple’s name was etched into history, he had sold many of his works for scraps. A hundred dollars. Two hundred dollars. Sometimes even less.

No blockchain.
No smart contracts.
No royalties.

As the NFT frenzy exploded, those early pieces resurfaced. Collectors flipped them on secondary markets, raking in tens of thousands of dollars per piece.

And Beeple?

He watched. Helpless. His art, his soul’s work, making fortunes for others, while he earned nothing from those resales.

A gap in the system. A creator’s nightmare.

In interviews, Beeple admitted it.
“Yes, I don’t get anything from those secondary sales”. That’s just how it was back then.

A digital revolution. But for Beeple’s early work, a cruel twist.

If Beeple Had @campnetworkxyz

The year is 2025. A new force rises. Camp Network.

A Layer-1 chain built for creators.

Beeple could have minted his art gas-free, embedding smart royalties from day one. Every resale, every flip, would have flowed value back to him.

Fans wouldn’t just follow. They would join his camp, complete quests, spread his art, and earn together.

No middlemen. No lost millions. Just power, in his hands.

And as the AI age dawned, Beeple’s camp could have licensed his work to AI agents, generating passive income, remixing his genius, always with his permission, always paying him back.

The Beeple we know changed art forever. But with @campnetworkxyz , he could have changed his fate too.

Power back to creators.

text:
Sam Parr sold The Hustle for $25M+. Now he’s building Hampton because he thinks communities are the next newsletters. Here’s why he’s right + how to build a $1M revenue community:

Why communities?

Traditional distribution is under threat:

• TikTok almost got banned this year
• Email is getting harder (low open rates due to pixel blocking, Gmail summary previews, spam filters)
• Social reach is throttled unless you pay to play

It's more important than ever to control your distribution—SMS, communities, events, etc.

Of course, communities are one of the hardest models to pull off.

But when they work, they work:

• Doximity (physicians): $570M • YPO (founders): $300M+
• Tiger 21 (HNW investors): $150M+
• Entrepreneurs organization (founders): $60M+
• Evanta: $23M profit, sold for $275M
• Hampton (founders): $10M+
• Client Ascension (agency owners): $4-$5M+
• Friends of Lenny’s Newsletter (product managers): $3-4M+
• Maker’s school (AI automation): $1.8M

…and many more

So, how do you build an engaging community?

1. Pick the right niche

The best communities either:

• Tap into high passions/careers (sneakers, nurses, engineers)
• Help members make money (ecomm, investing, ghostwriting)

The best ones do both.

2. Build where your members already hang out

It's extremely hard to build a community.

It's even harder to do it where your users don't naturally spend time.

Hampton and Client Ascension were built in Slack because they cater to founders who are already there.

Don't force your members onto Circle or Kajabi unless you have a 10x reason to.

3. Avoid the middle pricing

Either choose:

• Mass pricing ($100-200/yr) = scalable, or
• Premium pricing (>$1K) = high-touch, intimate

Avoid mid-tier pricing ($300-$700).

It's a dead zone.

Too expensive to scale (at $300/yr, you need 33K members to hit $10M), too cheap to justify the effort.

4. Treat onboarding as a product

The first 30 days should make the members feel they made the right decision.

Examples:

• Jay Clouse does 1:1 onboarding calls to help you connect with the right people/content.
• Client Ascension gives you a Day 1-35 roadmap, a coach pairing, and instant intros.

5. Lean on members + experts

You've aggregated distribution for valuable people.

Giving that distribution to members is enticing for them and saves you from 100% fulfillment. Win-win.

• Client Ascension has 7-figure coaches lead specialized calls.
• Hampton had member Anne Mahlum host an event at her house.

6. Gate access

Obsessing over fast growth kills the community. Once it declines, it's almost impossible to save it.

So, use filters — income, title, invite-only, industry — to protect and maintain strict quality.

Bonus: Have fun

Use 5–10% of your budget on “magical moments.”

Example: Shaan Puri used a Cameo from Sean Paul to welcome new members.
